tagline: Sync issues between Linear engineering and ClickUp project management
metaTitle: Linear + ClickUp Integration: Linear Status in ClickUp Tasks
metaDescription: Push Linear issue status to ClickUp tasks and create issues from ClickUp requirements. GAIA syncs sprint timelines. See the setup steps.
intro:
Engineering teams that use Linear for issue tracking often work alongside operations and project management teams running their work in ClickUp. Each tool suits its audience, but the boundary between them creates a handoff problem. Project managers cannot see when engineering tasks progress. Engineers cannot see when upstream dependencies managed in ClickUp change.

GAIA bridges the two so engineering velocity is visible to project managers and project context is visible in Linear. Status changes on issues propagate to their linked tasks automatically. When a task representing a product requirement is updated, GAIA flags the relevant issues so engineers know what changed without switching tools.

Teams that have tried to consolidate on a single tool and failed because different functions have strong preferences will find this integration especially valuable. GAIA lets each team work in their preferred tool while maintaining a shared source of truth that neither has to maintain manually.

useCases.title: Propagate issue status to ClickUp tasks
useCases.description: When a Linear issue moves to In Review or Done, GAIA updates the linked task status so project managers always have a real-time view of engineering progress without pinging engineers for updates.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from requirements tasks
useCases.description: When a product requirement task is approved and ready for development, GAIA creates corresponding issues with priority, description, and due date pre-populated from the task.

useCases.title: Sync ClickUp sprint timelines to Linear cycles
useCases.description: GAIA reads ClickUp sprint dates and creates matching cycles, ensuring engineering sprints are aligned with the delivery schedule tracked there, without manual date entry in both tools.

useCases.title: Alert engineers to scope changes
useCases.description: When a task that has linked issues is edited (priority changed, deadline shifted, requirements updated), GAIA posts a comment on the issue summarizing what changed so engineers are never surprised.

useCases.title: Roll up engineering metrics into project dashboards
useCases.description: GAIA periodically syncs cycle metrics (velocity, completion rate, lead time) into custom fields on the corresponding project so leadership can track engineering health alongside other project KPIs.

howItWorks.description: Connect both workspaces to GAIA. During setup, map Linear teams and projects to the corresponding ClickUp Spaces and Lists.

howItWorks.step: Set sync direction and field mappings
howItWorks.description: Define which fields are authoritative in which tool, which status values map between the two, and which events should trigger actions on the other side.
From that point on, GAIA monitors both tools and applies updates automatically. Engineers and project managers each work in their preferred tool with confidence that the other side stays current.

faqs.question: Can GAIA handle the different status models between Linear and ClickUp?
faqs.answer: Yes. During setup you provide a status mapping table — for example, the issue's In Progress maps to the task's In Development, and the issue's Done maps to the task's Completed. GAIA applies this mapping consistently so statuses are always semantically equivalent.

faqs.question: What happens to tasks that have no linked issue?
faqs.answer: GAIA only acts on tasks and issues that are explicitly linked or match your configured sync rules. Unlinked tasks are untouched. You can manually trigger issue creation from a task by assigning a specific label or status.

faqs.question: Is there a limit to how many issues GAIA can sync?
faqs.answer: GAIA's sync capacity scales with your plan. Most engineering teams sync hundreds to thousands of issues per month without hitting limits. For very large workspaces, you can scope sync to specific Lists or Tags to keep volume manageable.
